subject: orthopaedics
title: Skeletal dysplasias: FGFR3, brittle bones and storage

steps.tx: **Achondroplasia** follows a gain of function change in **FGFR3**, and most cases arise as new sporadic mutations. Limbs shorten most in the proximal **rhizomelic** segments, and the hand shows a trident gap between middle and ring fingers. The head looks large with frontal bossing and a flat midface, as this figure shows. Intelligence and lifespan stay normal, so counselling reassures while growth charts and sleep studies guide care.
steps.say: The figure shows a child whose limbs stay short while the head grows large. Proximal segments shorten most, which gives the pattern its recognised medical name. Fingers separate into a three pronged shape that clinicians call a trident hand. Most cases appear without any family history as a fresh genetic change. Normal intelligence and lifespan allow honest reassurance during family counselling sessions.

vis.alt: Diagram showing a child with achondroplasia, highlighting facial features, limb shortening, trident hand, and specific pelvic X-ray findings.
vis.caption: Achondroplasia: characteristic clinical and radiological features

steps.tx: **Osteogenesis imperfecta** weakens bone through faulty collagen, so fractures follow minimal trauma from early childhood. **Blue sclera**, abnormal teeth and hearing loss complete the classic triad beyond the bones. Type one disease stays mild, type two kills around birth, and type three deforms severely. **Bisphosphonate** therapy raises bone density, while telescoping rods grow with the child and reduce fractures.
steps.say: Faulty collagen makes the whole skeleton fragile from the earliest years of life. Minor falls then cause repeated fractures that heal in abnormal positions. The white of the eye looks blue because the underlying vessels show through. Teeth may look discoloured and hearing can fail as the child grows. Bone strengthening drugs and growing rods reduce fractures and deformity.

steps.tx: This skeletal survey shows **multiple healing fractures** with beaded ribs, and the insets add **blue sclera** and abnormal dentinogenesis. Together these features illustrate **osteogenesis imperfecta**, where faulty collagen weakens the whole skeleton. The image matters because fractures at different healing stages can mimic inflicted injury and need careful separation. For the exam, read the eye and teeth insets as part of one collagen disorder.
steps.say: The whole body film shows many fractures healing at different stages of repair. Ribs look beaded where repeated fractures have healed along the chest wall. Small insets show a blue tinted eye and discoloured abnormal teeth beside the film. Those features unite as one inherited disorder of collagen formation. Examiners value the combination because bone fragility alone has many possible causes.

vis.alt: Infant skeletal survey with fractures, beaded ribs, blue sclera and dentinogenesis insets.
vis.caption: Skeletal survey showing osteogenesis imperfecta fractures and features. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: **Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia** makes epiphyses small and irregular, while spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia flattens vertebrae as **platyspondyly**. Pseudoachondroplasia spares the face yet shortens limbs severely through a cartilage protein defect. Diastrophic dysplasia gives a hitchhiker thumb with clubfoot from birth. A full **skeletal survey** maps the pattern, and instability at the neck needs screening in at risk types.
steps.say: Growth plate disorders will shape the ends of bones and the spine in distinct patterns. Some conditions flatten every vertebral body while sparing the limbs relatively more. Others spare the face completely yet shorten the limbs very severely indeed. A thumb that points outward with clubfoot suggests one specific rare pattern. Whole skeleton films map the pattern and guide genetic referral accurately.

steps.tx: In **Hurler syndrome** absent enzyme activity clouds the cornea and coarsens the face, the gargoylism picture. **Hunter syndrome** follows X linked inheritance and troubles airway and behaviour more prominently. Films show a J shaped sella and paddle shaped ribs in the **dysostosis** pattern. Urine tests and enzyme assays confirm the diagnosis, and difficult airway planning protects these children at surgery.
steps.say: Storage material builds up inside cells and slowly distorts the face and skeleton. One syndrome will cloud the clear front window of the eye early in life. Another inherited form mainly affects boys and narrows the upper airway dangerously. Curved skull and rib changes give radiologists a recognisable pattern across films. Enzyme testing confirms the exact type and guides long term specialist care.
